meeting_header:
Date: 2026-02-27
Time: 15:00 UTC (scheduled 45-60 min slot)
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Morgan Blake (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Jia Li (Redwood CSM); Laura Chen (Ironclad Head of Security), Evan Morales (Infra Lead), Priya Nair (Compliance)
summary: Introductory security posture review focused on SOC 2/ISO artifacts, control-to-evidence traceability, Trust Center access, SSO/RBAC options, audit log retention, and KMS integration for data residency. Redwood provided an overview of what artifacts are available via the Trust Center and proposed next steps to validate private deployment feasibility and encryption handoff. Customer requested redacted SOC 2 Type II, clarifications on KMS flows for BYOK, and explicit audit log retention SLAs.
topics: Audit logs: retention, export, and access controls
Private deployment feasibility and pilot checkpoints
transcript:
[00:00] Morgan (AE): Hey folks, thanks for joining, really appreciate you taking the time. I'm Morgan from Redwood Inference, I'm the AE on this account. Uh, quick roll call?
[00:07] Laura (Ironclad): Hi Morgan, Laura here.
[00:09] Evan (Ironclad): Evan on my end.
[00:11] Priya (Ironclad): Priya standing by.
[00:13] Samir (SE): Samir here, Redwood SE.
[00:15] Jia (CSM): Jia from Customer Success.
[00:18] Morgan: Great. Agenda — we thought we'd run through a quick overview of the Trust Center artifacts, confirm the SOC 2 / ISO reports you need, talk control mapping and traceability out to evidence, then dig into SSO/RBAC and KMS/encryption flows. We'll leave time for Qs and then agree next steps. Does that sound right?
[00:33] Laura: Yep, that works. Our auditors will want traceability from control to specific logs/evidence, so that's the big ask. Also curious about how Redwood surfaces the evidence in the Trust Center - is it downloadable for auditors or is it portal-only?
[00:47] Morgan: Good question. Short answer: most artifacts are available as downloadable PDFs from the Trust Center, and we can provide a redacted SOC 2 Type II report on request. For some infra logs we provide exports — more on that in a bit.
[01:02] Samir: To add — we also have an evidence mapping doc that ties each control to example evidence buckets, e.g., access control policies -> SSO logs, change management -> deploy audit trail. It's not a per-customer prepopulated map for every control but we can share the template and work with you to map your controls.
[01:18] Evan: When you say SSO logs, are those session events or more like SAML assertion logs? Our internal auditors specifically look for assertion verification timestamps.
[01:27] Samir: We capture both. There's a bit of nuance: SAML assertions show up in our auth provider logs, which we can export, and session events are in the runtime traces. We can correlate them but sometimes the mapping requires a short mapping exercise.
[01:40] Priya: Can you speak to RBAC — admin separation, least privilege. We need to show users with admin rights and their access scope.
[01:48] Morgan: Yes, RBAC is surfaced in the Console — roles, role bindings, and recent role changes. For Dedicated/Private customers we offer more granular role scoping and can integrate with your IdP for SCIM provisioning.
[01:58] Laura: SCIM provisioning, perfect. Are role change audit events retained for how long? Our baseline is 1 year, prefer 3 for some sensitive orgs.
[02:07] Samir: Default retention in hosted is 90 days for verbose runtime traces, but audit logs and admin actions in the control plane are kept 13 months by default for enterprise plans; we can adjust retention with add-on log retention packages.
[02:20] Jia: And we do provide exports and an S3-compatible dump for long-term archival if you need to ship to your own bucket.
[02:26] Evan: Okay good. Another big one: KMS and BYOK. How does your key exchange look for private deployments? We can't have keys in Redwood-managed KMS for our regulated workloads.
[02:35] Samir: For Private deployments we support customer-managed keys. There's a couple of patterns: bring-your-own-key with a Cloud KMS (customer KMS) where we do a key wrap and never store plaintext; HSM integration for on-prem where the key material never leaves HSM. We'll send a design sketch.
[02:51] Laura: Can you detail the handshake? Like, does Redwood call out to our KMS at token time, or do you cache wrapped keys in your runtime?
[02:59] Samir: We do a short lived unwrap/derive on the instance at startup for performance; we never persist plaintext keys on disk. We’ve got a secure enclave pattern where keys are in memory, rotated per instance, and we log key usage in the audit trail. That's in our security whitepaper, we'll link.
[03:16] Morgan: Note that for hosted customers who require BYOK we typically route them to Dedicated or Private deployment options.
[03:22] Priya: For hosted — what's the minimum we need to provide for auditors to consider the evidence chain complete?
[03:29] Morgan: Usually it's: 1) SOC 2 Type II report and cover letter, 2) control mapping doc, 3) redacted logs/exports demonstrating samples, 4) Trust Center access for auditor accounts. That combination usually satisfies initial auditors; they sometimes ask follow-ups.
[03:45] Laura: Trust Center access for auditors — can auditors login directly under an auditor role or do we have to share artifacts?
[03:52] Morgan: We can grant auditor invites with read-only access scoped to specific artifacts. For some customers they prefer we deliver a bundle of artifacts to a secure S3 share instead. We can support both.
[04:03] Evan: About data residency — our EU customers' data must stay in eu-west-1. If we run workloads on Redwood, can we pin region and ensure caching/KV doesn't leak across regions?
[04:14] Samir: Yes, region pinning is supported in Dedicated and Private. For hosted we have region routing but prefix/KV cache occasionally resides in regional clusters; we can guarantee data locality for EU with dedicated capacity in the region. We'll need to capture the list of datasets you consider EU-only.
[04:29] Priya: We'll provide that list. On the SOC 2 report — do you share the full bridge letters or only Type II? Our auditors ask for bridge letters when there's a gap between report date and go-live.
[04:40] Morgan: We can share bridge letters where applicable. If there is an out-of-scope item we document compensating controls. We'll include the bridge letter if it exists for the most recent cycle.
[04:52] Laura: One pain point is traceability — our auditors ask for an index mapping every control to exact artifacts. How granular can Redwood be?
[05:00] Samir: We can provide a control matrix template pre-populated with example evidence paths. For Dedicated/Private we can go deeper and map to your audit exports — timestamps, log IDs, and SAML assertion IDs. For hosted, we provide the standard examples but can work with you to attach customer-specific exports.
[05:18] Priya: How about chain-of-custody for evidence — is there an access log for artifact downloads? Auditors want to see who accessed a report and when.
[05:27] Jia: The Trust Center records artifact access and download events, with user and timestamp; we log auditor access and can include that as part of the evidence bundle.
[05:35] Evan: If we integrate our IdP with SAML + SCIM, do you support enforced MFA for admin roles?
[05:42] Samir: Yes, we can enforce MFA via IdP policies for admin role access. For Redwood-managed accounts we support TOTP and hardware keys. For SSO-backed logins, MFA enforcement flows through your IdP.
[05:55] Laura: Ok, last big topic: audit log export format and retention — do you provide structured logs? Some of our tooling wants JSON lines with specific fields.
[06:03] Samir: Exports are JSONL with configurable schema. We have a mapping doc for fields (timestamp, user_id, action, resource, request_id). We can add extra fields in a private deployment if needed.
[06:16] Morgan: Quick pause — any other questions before we talk next steps?
[06:20] Priya: One quick one — do you have a sample control mapping for ISO 27001 as well or only SOC 2?
[06:25] Samir: We have both. The ISO mapping sits alongside the SOC 2 matrix in the Trust Center; we can provide the ISO mapping and the overlap matrix.
[06:33] Laura: Great. Would like to see a redacted Type II and then schedule a technical deep-dive on the KMS integration and the audit log export schema.
[06:41] Morgan: Perfect. We'll send the redacted report and a short checklist for the KMS deep-dive. Jia will coordinate scheduling.
[06:48] Jia: I'll follow up with proposed times for the week of March 9th.
[06:52] Evan: One last thing — pricing impacts for increased retention and S3 export? Can you ballpark?
[06:58] Morgan: Rough numbers: +20% for 12 months to 13 months retention is often included; longer retention and S3 archival add-on is usage-based — we'll send an estimate in the pricing doc.
[07:09] Laura: Okay thanks.
[07:11] Morgan: Alright let's wrap.
[07:13] Samir: Thanks everyone.
[07:15] Jia: Thanks all, notes and next steps will come through.
[07:18] [end 48:00]

Notes on quality: There are occasional mis-hearings in the transcript; product names and acronyms may be slightly garbled (e.g., "S3 dump" transcribed as "S3 hump" in one excerpt). The technical details are high level; the SE promised a deeper engineering session to go through KMS key wrap patterns and audit export schema in detail.
